# Installing R{.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 1 &middot; PART A]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

## Four ways to get R

| Route | Good for | The catch |
|---|---|---|
| Distro packages (`apt`, `yum`) | One R, kept current by the OS | One version at a time; version follows the distro |
| Posit's [r-builds](https://github.com/rstudio/r-builds) / [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig) | Several versions side by side under `/opt/R/<version>` | You own the upgrade cadence |
| Build from source | Full control of flags, BLAS, `--prefix` | You own the build, the toolchain, and the reproducing of it |
| Container images (`rocker/*`) | Reproducible, disposable | Persisting user libraries needs thought, calling other programs from R via `system2()` requires programs being installed in the docker image |

## The one rule that saves you later

::: {.note}
[Rule]{.note-label}

- Never install a new R version into the same directory as an existing one,
  where it overwrites the old version's files in place.
- Never point two R versions at the same package library.
:::

Packages are compiled against a specific R. We come back to libraries in
block 2.

## Building from source

```bash
curl -LO https://cran.r-project.org/src/base/R-4/R-4.6.1.tar.gz
tar xf R-4.6.1.tar.gz
cd R-4.6.1

./configure --help
./configure --prefix=/opt/R/4.6.1 \
            --enable-R-shlib \
            --enable-memory-profiling

make -j"$(nproc)"
make check          # optional, and slow, and worth it once
make install
```

Important flags:

- `--prefix` is what makes versioned side-by-side installs work.
- `--enable-R-shlib` builds `libR.so`
  ([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Configuration-options)).
  Without it, RStudio Server, Workbench, and anything else that embeds R
  (such as Python's `rpy2`) will not work
  ([Posit docs](https://docs.posit.co/resources/install-r-source.html)).

## Optimization flags

`configure` accepts the usual compiler variables, and R records them so every
package you compile later inherits them.

```bash
./configure --prefix=/opt/R/4.6.1 --enable-R-shlib \
  CFLAGS="-O2 -g" \
  CXXFLAGS="-O2 -g"
```

::: {.note}
[Avoid]{.note-label}
`-march=native` lets the compiler use every instruction the build machine's
CPU supports, so the result might not run on other machines
([GCC](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/x86-Options.html#index-march-13)).
Build in a container on a newer host, run on an older node, and packages die
with `Illegal instruction`. If you need a target, name one, such as
`-march=x86-64-v2`.
:::

`-O2` is what `configure` picks by default for GCC
([Autoconf](https://www.gnu.org/software/autoconf/manual/autoconf-2.72/html_node/C-Compiler.html)).
`-ffast-math` gives up IEEE guarantees that R's `NA`, `NaN` and `Inf` handling
relies on ([GCC](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Optimize-Options.html#index-ffast-math)).

## Where those flags end up

`configure` bakes them into `Makeconf`, which every later `R CMD INSTALL`
reads. This is the file to check when a user's compile behaves oddly.

```bash
R CMD config CC
R CMD config CFLAGS
R CMD config --all | head -30

# the file itself
grep -E '^(CFLAGS|CXXFLAGS|FFLAGS) ' "$(R RHOME)/etc/Makeconf"
cat "$(R RHOME)/etc/Makeconf"
```

A site can override any of it per-installation in
`$(R RHOME)/etc/Makevars.site`, and a user can override that in
`~/.R/Makevars`
([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Customizing-package-compilation-1)).
Both are worth knowing about, because both are places a
"works for me, not for them" difference hides.

## BLAS and LAPACK

Many models rely on linear algebra. R ships a
reference BLAS and can instead link to a tuned one ([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#BLAS-1)).

| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| Reference BLAS (default) | Used unless an external BLAS is requested at configure time |
| OpenBLAS | Serial, threaded and OpenMP builds packaged by Fedora and Debian; picks CPU-specific code at run time ([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#OpenBLAS-and-BLIS)) |
| Intel MKL | For Intel processors; ships its own tuned LAPACK; Intel's link line advisor is recommended |
| Apple Accelerate | macOS; differs from the reference BLAS on `NA` vs `NaN`, and many packages fail their checks with it |

```bash
./configure --prefix=/opt/R/4.6.1 --enable-R-shlib \
            --with-blas="-lopenblas" --with-lapack
```

## BLAS: the two catches {.skip}

**Threading.** Threaded builds of OpenBLAS take their thread count from
`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS` or `OMP_NUM_THREADS`
([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#OpenBLAS-and-BLIS)). A multi-threaded BLAS can take more CPU
time and even more elapsed time than a single-threaded one, and other work
on the machine competes with it
([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Linear-algebra-1)). Nest it inside `parallel::mclapply()` and
the competition is with itself. Pin it site-wide in `Renviron.site`:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
```

**Reproducibility.** BLAS implementations that compute in parallel can be
non-deterministic ([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#BLAS)): results can differ between runs on
the same machine. For most work this is irrelevant; for a regulatory
submission it is a finding.

::: {.note}
[Check what you actually have]{.note-label}
`sessionInfo()` reports the BLAS and LAPACK in use, and
`extSoftVersion()[["BLAS"]]` gives the path
([`?sessionInfo`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/sessionInfo.html)). Run these on any server you
inherit. Installations surprise people.
:::

```r
extSoftVersion()[["BLAS"]]
```

```text
[1] "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openblas-pthread/libblas.so.3"
```

Our lab container is already on OpenBLAS: the `rocker/r-base` Dockerfile
installs `libopenblas0-pthread`
([Dockerfile](https://github.com/rocker-org/rocker/blob/master/r-base/latest/Dockerfile)).

## Capabilities: what the build can do

A build's features depend on what was present at `configure` time.

```r
capabilities()
```

```text
       jpeg         png        tiff       tcltk         X11        aqua
       TRUE        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE       FALSE       FALSE
   http/ftp     sockets      libxml        fifo      cledit       iconv
       TRUE        TRUE       FALSE        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE
        NLS       Rprof     profmem       cairo         ICU long.double
       TRUE        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE
    libcurl
       TRUE
```

See `?capabilities` for more information.

## Our lab installation

We are not going to build R from source in the workshop as that would take too long given the available time.

```bash
docker run --rm -it --name rlab rocker/r-base bash
```

`rocker/r-base` is Debian (currently `forky/sid`) with R from the Debian
packages. That makes it a realistic stand-in for a distro-installed R, which
is what most of you have.

::: {.note}
[If you are on Apple silicon]{.note-label}
The image is `linux/amd64` only, so Docker runs it emulated and you will see
a platform warning. Everything works; compiles are much slower.
:::
